word.title: Tapestry Link Names A Node
word.description: Every tapestry: link in the markdown of the instance's own nodes names a node in this graph.

graphRule.name: tapestry-link-names-a-node
graphRule.says: every `tapestry:` link in the markdown of the instance's own nodes names a node in this graph. Its key is the key of a node in this graph other than a change entry or a tag, whatever the point of view. A `tapestry:` link means "in this graph" (ADR graph-rules/0002, Decision 2), so a key no such node has is a dead link, such as one to a node deleted since, or a key from another instance.
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the instance's own nodes (D4). Links in other people's letters are left alone, and a `nostr:` link to a node this graph doesn't hold isn't judged, since its letter may be on a relay.
graphRule.refusesOrReports: it only reports. `graph delete-node` leaves the links to a node dead, and a renderer is to show a dead link as its text (ADR graph-rules/0002, Decision 4).
graphRule.check: a check finds each `tapestry:` link in the markdown of the instance's own nodes, reading a value held as an `lmdb:` pointer from the text it resolves to (ADR graph-rules/0002, Decision 6), and names each link whose key no such node has, with the node that holds it. It reads markdown with a CommonMark parser, so that examples in code aren't read as links and reference definitions are (the ADR's Implementation notes). `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph.
graphRule.repair: none yet. `graph update-node` changes an element's fields, and `graph update-concept` a concept's description: point the link at a node that exists, or make it plain text.
